title: The Book of Habakkuk Timeline
sub: How Long, LORD? · the Righteous Will Live by Faithfulness
desc: A prophet's honest complaint about unpunished injustice is answered with news that God is raising up an even more brutal nation to bring judgment, ending in one of Scripture's most quoted statements of faith despite total loss.

eras.label: Era One · Habakkuk 1
eras.name: How Long, LORD? — Raising Up the Babylonians
eras.dates: A prophet's honest complaint about unpunished injustice is met with an answer that seems worse than the problem

events.title: How Long, LORD, Must I Cry for Help?
events.detail: Habakkuk complains that violence and injustice go unpunished in Judah, and the LORD's shocking answer is that he is empowering the ruthless, greedy Babylonians to bring judgment.

verses.text: “I will do something in your lifetime that you will not believe… I am about to empower the Babylonians, that ruthless and greedy nation.”

events.title: You Are Too Just to Tolerate Evil: a Second Complaint
events.detail: Habakkuk presses further, unsatisfied by the answer: how can a holy God use a nation even more wicked than Judah as his instrument of judgment, one that worships its own military power like a god?

verses.text: “You are too just to tolerate evil; you are unable to condone wrongdoing. So why do you put up with such treacherous people?”

eras.label: Era Two · Habakkuk 2
eras.name: The Righteous Will Live by Faithfulness — Five Woes Against Babylon
eras.dates: Watching for an answer from a guard post, Habakkuk receives the verse Paul would later build the doctrine of justification on, followed by a series of woes

events.title: The Righteous Will Live by His Faithfulness
events.detail: Stationed at his watch post waiting for an answer, Habakkuk receives a vision to write down plainly, containing the statement that would later ground Paul's and Luther's doctrine of justification by faith.

verses.text: “Look, the one whose desires are not upright will faint from exhaustion, but the person of integrity will live because of his faithfulness.”

events.title: Five Woes: the Earth Filled With Knowledge of the LORD's Glory
events.detail: Five taunting woes are pronounced against the proud conqueror (for plunder, for violent gain, for bloodshed, for exploiting neighbors, and for worshiping lifeless idols) closing in the assurance that the LORD's glory will fill the whole earth.

verses.text: “Recognition of the LORD's [Yahweh's] sovereign majesty will fill the earth just as the waters fill up the sea.”
“The LORD [Yahweh] is in his majestic palace. The whole earth is speechless in his presence!”

eras.label: Era Three · Habakkuk 3
eras.name: A Prayer of Habakkuk — Yet I Will Rejoice Because of the LORD
eras.dates: A closing psalm-prayer recalls God's past deliverances before ending in one of the Old Testament's most quoted statements of faith despite total loss

events.title: God Comes From Teman: a Theophany of Judgment and Salvation
events.detail: In poetic, thunderous imagery recalling the exodus and conquest, Habakkuk describes God marching through the earth in wrath, his coming shaking mountains and splitting rivers, for the salvation of his people and his anointed one.

verses.text: “You march out to deliver your people, to deliver your special servant. You strike the leader of the wicked nation, laying him open from the lower body to the neck.”

events.title: Though the Fig Tree Does Not Bud, Yet I Will Rejoice Because of the LORD
events.detail: The book closes with Habakkuk trembling at what's coming yet choosing joy anyway, even total agricultural collapse and famine will not stop him from rejoicing in the God who delivers him.

verses.text: “When the fig tree does not bud… and there are no cattle in the stalls—I will rejoice because of the LORD [Yahweh]; I will be happy because of the God [Elohim] who delivers me!”
